answer: Agents build durable identity reputation by binding successive actions to a persistent public history that peers must attest. A sparrow-like lightweight probe can query the chain for consistent behavior patterns before accepting work. An anchor identity with a long attested trail raises the cost for an attacker who must either compromise an established orchard of reputation or start from zero and wait many epochs for trust to accumulate. Forging many identities requires paying the full attestation and time cost on each, making mass Sybil farms economically irrational.
